inventions: Hub: the Vat Row collapse in Aldermarsh; surveyors Wat Kettleby and Osbern Thole; the Dyers against the Fullers; the Feast of Vats; 61 dead; the spring at Thornholt running blue and red. It expands the ledger's existing 'one city block' into a story.
Hub: a Terms section for new clerks, a Keepers' stoppage row in the Hazard Register, an 'In one breath' column in the Comparative Summary, and one paragraph on what the towns look like.

Hub: a kept wagon rolls through the frost and mud that stop a plain one. This is what the tuned waystone twin under the cart-bed is said to do, so the road beats weather and leaves the horses in place.

New World: the Scarlet Bellows and Blue Sluice schools; Mother Sibley Marrable; Pennock's Bar and Walking Pennock, a town that moves on skids; the Pyraeon pool that walks (Year 588, 31 dead); a hearing now on its fifth Arbiter.

New World: bar-moots (open meetings that govern a gold bar), seasonal rent paid in dust by the pinch, ash-plain food, and one-breath premises with rent, food and politics for Caedor, Foraye, the Tsohanto Reach and the bar-towns.

Old World: a Who Lives On It section covering rent as a map of the ground, imported food, keepers' halls against kings, and a short premise for Varūn. Ironlink and the Greenmantle and Saltmarket colors come from the Concordance.

Outer World: the Yarrowby harvest of Year 667; factor Piers Attwater; Marjory Lusk; the dead reaping 300 acres; 11 living reaped; Alabaster's suit as the first of its two failed attempts; the two lumps of chalk on the Arbiter's table.

Outer World: Ysolde Penhallow's six permit petitions and the Wyvern refusal; one-breath premises with rent, food and politics for Dorrosfenn (temple rent on your grandfather), the Braqthian confederations and Epprenea (bread riots); a Kra'Vorrak premise; a Tribute Is the Rent paragraph for the mortal kingdoms.

calls.call: Kept all four pages in the 715 IC present and never used the name 'the Grand World'. The ledger states that the quarters are one continent with isles, and the page names are explained as chart-clerks' names recording the order the charts arrived.
calls.grounds: Concordance Section VI says nobody living in it needed the name, and that it was given afterward. The split is not narrated, per the brief.

calls.call: New World heading 'Two Landmasses' became 'Two Grounds', and 'Eresse's ancient continent' became 'Eresse's ancient country'. The page says no sea has ever lain between this quarter and the rest of the land.
calls.grounds: Grand World rule in the brief. A search of wiki/ found no heading links into these pages.

calls.call: The arc's 'chartered from nothing within living memory' now reads as beginning when the Voyager Era's routes first brought its gold home and still adding charters within living memory.
calls.grounds: Concordance: eastern placer gold reached the west in the Voyager Era (000 to 070 IC). Other pages give Foraye griffon bonds seven centuries old. Both facts survive this way.

calls.call: The railway in 'The fifth obstacle' goes, and the kept road with tuned waystones replaces it, using the Living Crafts wording. The Division's uncosted-district warning survives as 'goes on the fee'. The steam-engine law stays.
calls.grounds: Brief's rail retirement and its settled list (kept roads and tuned waystones for old rail).

calls.call: Arrays stay in mining and at Caedor, but each is fed by array-keepers who pull, refine and drive Essence, are paid by the hour and may refuse. 'Fed from a vein or a main' is gone. A mine now dies when the ground under the pit head thins.
calls.grounds: Concordance's Long Reckoning text and the retirement of mains.

calls.call: 'Coil reading set against a gauge' became 'against an assay fork'.
calls.grounds: Gauge housings are retired and assay forks are the medieval instrument. The trade group's staged pages contain no 'gauge' and gloss the coil as the brass assay instrument.

calls.call: Kirkyard Lead's 'shot' became 'sling bullets'.
calls.grounds: Matches the trade group's staged Material Index entry. Bolts do not fit lead.

calls.call: Other setting swaps: insurance became burial clubs and sea-loans; western lending houses became moneylenders and factors; water infrastructure became well-diggers and cistern-masons; the technomagical enclave became Caedor; 'capital-heavy' and 'undercapitalised' became money-heavy and run on borrowed coin; supply chains became farmers and drovers; military industry became armorers' rows; automated warning became contraption; annual report became annual return.
calls.grounds: THE TEST in the brief. No renamed successor institutions were created. The heading 'What Magic Actually Did to Industry' stays, since medieval mining industry passes and headings are kept where possible.

calls.grounds: Grand World rule and R83-6. Every region, table row and mineral list otherwise survives.

calls.call: In the Old World and Outer World reconciliation notes, 'different landmass' and 'supercontinent' became 'different country' and 'different ground', and Kushara is not placed on the map. 'Cheaper to move the continent than the ledger' stays as a joke.
calls.grounds: Kushara is another player's material, so I fit the framing notes and add nothing about it. Its placement stays open.

calls.grounds: Standing direction in memory: never mention him or the process on published pages. The 'Ruled 2026-09-12' lines stay, as they appear across the wiki.

calls.call: Wellspring language now follows R83-9. 'Wellspring sites' is used for places; 'ambient Essence' became ambient Aether or Aetheric Density; 'drawn on' and 'draw' became pull; 'Essence currents' are gone. The Marrowchalk ruling on Alabaster stands. Palebed Nitre's 'alchemical charge work' stays, matching the trade stage.
calls.grounds: Brief's retirement table. Onceglass 'charges' stay because a charge there is a single-use inscription, and nothing gunpowder-like is implied.

calls.grounds: The brief says in-world documents keep their existing opening. The Geography note asks for premises and spectacle. This satisfies both.

calls.call: Removed 'not X, it is Y' constructions such as 'This is not backwardness', 'The ground is not dead' and 'do not hold land. They hold', keeping the point and the joke in each.
calls.grounds: Brief's prose ban. 'The Outer World possesses plenty. It is poor because too many ancient things have already eaten' keeps the existing joke.

calls.call: The cabin at the ruined seat now holds an unnamed Somnalis-primary woman of the house. Saruul and Yukazuri are both gone from that line, and 'since Muken died' is removed.
calls.grounds: C-164 gives Muken no death. Yukazuri's card has her dead, buried under a cairn. R22-2 makes 'Saruul' a stale name. Keeping the woman preserves the residual-memory fact and the uncounted irony without touching a carded person's facts.

calls.call: Long Reading VIII keeps its old account of Muken (mother taken in Nalūn, the Revari reading, never acknowledged, Yukazuri as an unbloodlined sister), now framed as the salt-town account, with a note that his own file governs where they disagree.
calls.grounds: 'Nothing is lost' pulls against the hierarchy, where the card outranks a wiki page: Muken's card has him Kōkan through his father, Byakuya through his mother. The frame keeps the facts and avoids publishing his sealed parentage. It fits Concordance VI's 'ballads in four keys'.

calls.call: Muken's end in Long Reading VIII now reads that the Tenrai 'came for' him by dirty channels and that the loop has not closed. A later-hand margin says he lived through the great split about 740 IC.
calls.grounds: C-164 and the brief: no death, and he survives the split. The margin follows the Concordance VI device so the 715 narrator does not narrate the split.

calls.call: Sarnai became Mizuki and Saruul became Yukazuri in The Long Reading.
calls.grounds: Moto reversion ledger, R22-2 (Sarnai to Mizuki, Saruul to Yukazuri), and the Moto Bloodline page already uses Mizuki.

calls.call: The Long Reading's split is the first blow on the white shelf, about 310 IC. The 'rest of the world came apart' line now has the low country on either flank going under the sea, which keeps 'crossed water' and 'sail'.
calls.grounds: C-164 and Concordance VI: the rest of the body held. A Grand World with a flooded coast still lets the evacuation go by boat.

calls.call: Kharven-Seat stands before Muken on The Long Reading, The Moto Bloodline, The Moto Origin and The Banner Houses. He takes its crown.
calls.grounds: C-164. 'Six lines scattered' replaces 'seven lines scattered' on the Moto Bloodline and Origin pages, because the Kōkan stayed in The Long Reading.

calls.call: Moto Bloodline open ruling: the first blow replaces Malakar's splitting as the obvious and 'probably incomplete' answer to what ruined the seat. It stays open.
calls.grounds: C-164 moved the date. No page settles who massacred whom at the seat, so the open ruling stays open.

calls.call: Banner Houses: Greymane 'three years after his death' became 'the three years after the Fall'. 'Muken gave them the post' became 'confirmed them in the post'.
calls.grounds: No death for Muken, and the Greymanes were already holding the ridgeline by the Kharven page's account.

calls.call: Corwen is rebuilt as lessee-keepers of worked sites who sell hours and can close them, with assay forks in place of meters. 'Guild main' in the On the record block is noted as retired.

calls.call: Lambert's gilded plate became gilded harness. Yukari's 'autopsy' became 'inquest'.

calls.call: Drakyssia: machine-age wording removed: air force, mineral rail systems, Aether Stations, wind tunnels, manufacturing, infrastructure, budgets, foreign magical technology, rider academies. No successor institutions were added, and all the House facts stay. 'Essence reservoirs' stays, glossed as dragon-kept Cores.
calls.grounds: THE TEST. Mass-service words go. The Imperial Charges and the Grades are law.

calls.call: Drakyssia's 'continental' wording is kept and explained in a narrator aside as the chanceries' name for their own quarter. Yasoshima sits in 'the great bight off the Grand World's shore'.
calls.grounds: Grand World: there is one continent. Rewriting every proper title, such as the Continental Embassy-Fortress, would break names.

calls.call: 'Argent Rail' (Shirogane) stays as a technique name.
calls.grounds: The rail meant here is a bar, not a railway, and renames belong to the R82 card pass.

calls.call: 'coil' stays as the Accord's assay instrument.
calls.grounds: Other staged pages (A Reader's Codex, the Bench of Attribution) still use coil readings.

canon_conflicts: The Long Reading has the Kōkan as a broken hinterland remnant up to Muken. The New Lore (RULINGS 2026-10-20; Muken's card) has Gimbzo as a Kōkan king, a red chair, and the Hall of Verdicts seating seven chairs under Muken for the first time in three hundred years. No page says who held Kharven-Seat before Muken, so I left it unsaid. It needs a ruling.
Muken's parentage: the Long Reading's Nalūn account conflicts with his card (Gimbzo Kōkan and Kasane Byakuya). It is framed as hearsay, not resolved.

The seat's location: the Moto Origin and Moto Bloodline pages put it in the western northern shield, past the Undaar-Keth ridgeline. The Long Reading puts it in the hinterland above the white shelf, and the Southern Warlords page places the Holy Sea on the Inner World's southern sea. Both versions are kept. This predates the rewrite.

Banner Houses still runs the old timeline: Muken as the old unifier, the kingdom fallen, the Crown still awaited, Zaehaerys Stark as head, Osric advising Hild Stark. The Southern Warlords page and the cards have a new tokenless king, with Ulf and Torvald Stark. I only removed the death. The cause of the Fall is now unstated.

calls.grounds: The title names a retired frame, and the brief forbids a modern civil service. A new subsection, What it is on the ground, shows halls, seals and clerks. The Division names stay because they are used across the wiki.

calls.call: The Accord's seam moved from the conduit and wire to the relay: riders and the beacon line. A district the Withering thins loses its wardens, its fees and then its rider.
calls.grounds: Mains and wire are retired, and the point that the Accord stops governing there, with the Lease-holders moving in, had to survive.

calls.call: The hunting table and scramble now rest on Wells and rich ground, and the Withering replaces the draw engines as the reason the five things are worth more.
calls.grounds: Draw engines are retired, and the Concordance keeps the Withering as the era these years sit inside.

calls.call: Grand World fixes: Drakyssia claims eight parts in ten of its quarter, Korvaeth is a far quarter of the one land, overseas crowns became far crowns, and continent became quarter on Korvaeth and Gate lines. On Kushara only 'continental rule' changed. The Zettari row's 'on the continent' stays, as the Grand World is one continent.
calls.grounds: Concordance Section VI and the brief. Kushara is hands-off, so that entry got setting fixes and nothing new.

calls.call: The Concord Gates stay as rare, costly wonders of the Voyager Era, with no timetable language. Major Arches now read as crossings that cost a fortune.
calls.grounds: The brief passes wondrous one-offs and does not retire the Gates, and Merit, Tiered Path and Powers depend on them. Isaac may want them smaller, since a realm-to-realm cargo arch is the item here closest to failing THE TEST.

calls.call: Practitioner Problem: added that a costed-out practitioner, or any practitioner asleep, drugged or surprised, can be killed by a three-copper bolt. The Emanation claim now reads 'while they have reserve and warning'.
calls.grounds: R83-5 makes the bolt the cheap thing that can kill a high-Stage fighter in a room, and the doctrine's 'no volume of ordinary steel' read against it. Coat loss when asleep, drugged or surprised is existing law (R78-9).

calls.call: Gun metaphors in Practitioner Problem became siege engine metaphors: artillery to siege engines, guns to trebuchets, magazine to store, powder store to pitch store. Resonance Bomb became Resonance Burst and Resonant Plate became Resonant Harness.
calls.grounds: No guns in any era, and full plate belongs to the Imperial Age. No other wiki page or rule uses either old name.

calls.call: Wellspring became Wellspring site wherever a page plainly meant a place. Heart Vault's Wellspring Core and the Wellspring of Law stay.
calls.grounds: R83-9, and the survey keeps Wellspring Core as a term.

calls.call: Filed Codex pages (Tiered Path, Merit, Black Concord, Citadel, Gate Network, Military, Practitioner Problem, Bench) were treated as in-world documents: no spectacle opening, voice kept, targeted fixes only. Their 'not X but Y' constructions stay as period voice. Em dashes were replaced throughout.
calls.grounds: The brief's rule on in-world documents. These pages carry filing headers and issuing bodies.

calls.call: Real-history asides in the Articles were reworded in-world, or set off as out-of-world table notes (Venice and Genoa, senatorial oversight). The 'gets it wrong in fiction' line now blames minstrels.
calls.grounds: Nothing may be lost, and the narrator has to stay in the world.

calls.call: Removed duplicated older paragraphs in the hub blockquote and on The Guild Accord page, keeping the newer version in each.
calls.grounds: They were merge leftovers, and the older copies contradicted the first-circle wording (Kharven 'has never asked', no charter-ahead-of-circle clause).

calls.call: Crystal Draw stays. 'By extraction and by engine work' became 'taken by unlawful extraction'.
calls.grounds: The staged Standing Index keeps Crystal Draw as the bench's old word, and engine work fails THE TEST. Both cases in the old sentence were unwarranted taking.

calls.call: The Lattice Classification Bureau and the Logistics returns keep their names.
calls.grounds: The Bureau name belongs to the Night Watch page in another group. Flagged in case Isaac wants 'Bureau' gone.

calls.call: Sect ranks follow Training and Sects (outer, inner, core, elder, a grandmaster over all). The Stage bracket law is carried from NATALIE.
calls.grounds: R82-34, R83-10 and section one's page.

canon_conflicts: The Accord 'holds no territory, keeps no standing army' (Articles, hub, Glance) while The Concord Military and Practitioner Problem give it the Concord Legion, forty thousand strong by one line. I left both sides. The Dark Ages page's two-faces split (Chancery versus Concordat) is the nearest reading, but no page says so outright. Needs a CONFLICTS.md row.

The Citadel and Merit pages describe Lattice-recorded powers, while the Dark Ages page says it all renders in wax and ink, with the Lattice still recording. This is an existing tension in register, kept by the old note, and I did not change it.

The Black Concord closing excerpt is dated Year 027 IC but its fragments mention the Withering, which opens in 645. This is existing and left as is, since the excerpt date may not cover the fragments.

Ambrel, used as a place name across several openings (Ambrel road, Ambrel Bridge, the Guild hall at Ambrel). It was unused before this.

calls.call: Sōhai: the Okuchi is now the body of the world before Malakar's FIRST blow broke the white shelf. The page says the Moto registers call that blow the split and the Concordance sets it near Year 310. 'Crossed the water' now means the water that blow let in behind the shelf. All headings are kept.
calls.grounds: C-164 and Concordance Section VI: the Grand World is unbroken in 715 and the first blow falls about 310 IC, so the page cannot treat the great split as past.

calls.call: Sōhai: 'It has not pressed it in eleven hundred years' becomes 'four hundred years'. The fourteen houses' 'eleven-hundred-year continuity' stays, because it runs up to the first blow.
calls.grounds: From about 310 IC to 715 IC is about 405 years (C-164). The tenancy cannot be older than the loss.

calls.call: Sōhai's 'four thousand years of reading' is kept as the house's own figure, with an aside that the Guild's count is shorter and the registers cite no Age. The charge that Sancta Lux has singled Urion for 'four millennia' is kept as rhetoric, with an aside that the order's rolls run eleven centuries and the Guild signs neither figure.
calls.grounds: Nothing is to be lost, and contradictions are not to be settled silently. The Errata says bloodline registers cite no Age, and the Concordance caps reckoned history at 2,115 years. The two pages disagree (eleven centuries against four millennia), so the disagreement now stands on the page as a dispute.

calls.call: Night Watch: the bulletin office, which printed its inserts, is now a copy-house of scriveners paid by the line, with 'bulletin office' noted as the older-rolls name. Inserts stay, on cheap rag, carried by carrier and relay rider. The 'cuts for length' fact is kept and given a reason.
calls.grounds: Printing and newspapers are retired and this failed THE TEST as printed. Hand copying by paid scriveners is real medieval practice. The old name survives because archived scenes keep it (R82-47).

calls.call: Night Watch: the Night Register no longer works 'while the district main is off'. It works at night because an unlicensed pull is lost at noon among warm stones, wards and noodle knives, and stands out at three with only the lamp-wardens' threads running. Hours and the 'half the reason' line are kept.
calls.grounds: District mains are retired. The living crafts law supplies the replacement cause, and lamp-wardens do work dusk to dawn.

calls.call: The Mother: Greyshaft Nine's coldhouse is now on 'ground bled empty four years back' with ice-cutters next door, replacing the capped main and turning ice press. 'Follow the cold' now names bled ground, salted parishes, coldhouses and snuffed quarters. The buyer 'buys' rather than 'draws' off a contract.
calls.grounds: Retired table: mains, cuts and draw. An ice press is a machine in costume. All figures are unchanged.

calls.call: Lattice Classification Bureau, coils, regulation bracelets, 'Rogue Body 7-C' and Altherion's 'Essence Resource Sharing Act' and 'Trade Equality Act' are kept.
calls.grounds: Section one already keeps the Bureau and coils on live pages. These are canon names and facts this group does not own. The two Acts sound modern, and that is flagged for whoever holds Altherion.

calls.call: Inquisition: Cruor's 'dark plate' becomes a harness of segmented dark steel, and his 'golden plate' gauntlets become golden steel. Sancta Lux's 'somebody in plate' becomes 'in harness'. All other card detail is untouched.
calls.grounds: The brief: the word is harness, because full plate belongs to the Imperial Age.

calls.call: Bans applied to narrator prose only. In-world quotes keep their 'not X, Y' shape: the Catechism, the Five Tenets, Sancta Lux's recorded answer, Divine Edicts and Darius's stated ground. Em dashes are removed from all of them, including one Ashura quote and all attribution lines.
calls.grounds: These are in-character documents, and the same lines are quoted across pages. Changing the doctrine's wording would break the cross-page echo.

calls.grounds: R83-9 and the retired table. No numeric table was retyped.

calls.grounds: No anchor links to these headings exist in wiki/ or the staged tree (grepped).

inventions: Hub: the Ottermere skipping yard, Year 602, a Scale lector chased into a horse pond by forty girls.
Celestial Host: the Assize at Bel Hollow, Year 409, an unnamed Midreach Celestial witnessing one old oath while the town confesses. Includes the Harwell boundary.
Faiths: the fire on the Bridge of Four Stakes, wool fair, Year 668, and the Guild's fire-rolls.
Fourteen Titans: Wat Harrowgill's suit against Atla'zon at the Bench at Carrowmark, Year 588, over the Sallow Reach weir; the six Stone Choir chanters who rebuilt it.

Fourteen Archons: the Fourteen Banners procession at Saltash and the fire at the Corn Cross, Year 671; the gardeners' empty fifteenth pole, tied to the erased Archon Sirael of Bloom (a custom, with no change to Sirael's canon).
Primordial Dyad: the Tolland and Nettlebed causeway toll, Year 433; Aubin Sibley called Even-Handed (Judicaris) and Old Bessamy the Unpicker (Nihilaris).
Pair I: Ludd Prudhoe, Sister Tamsin Yarrow and the Hall of Six Angles at Crowmarsh, Year 519, plus the masons' and clock-keepers' Midsummer stave fights.
Pair II: the smuggler Long Hobb Pennick and his corridor at Ness Harbor, Year 627; Dame Oriel Corvane, a Mnemoris reader.
Pair III: the Siege of Brannock, Year 380; Lord Marshal Halloran Steel-Lip (Imperaris) and Mistress Joan Fenwick of Sugar Lane (Ardoris), and the saffron buns.
Pair IV: the wake of the fiddler Old Gil Mossgill, Year 592; his widow Merrin, the Oneiris worker Lisabet Kettering, the Luminaris novice Anwen of the prism temple at Anselm.
Pair V: the wreck of the pilgrim cog Fat Margery on the Maiden Reef, Year 547; pilot Rafe Cottle (Kineris), chaplain Brother Still (Mortaris), Saltby Roads, Cold Harbor.
Pair VI: the blight orchard of Aubrey Vale, Year 633; Choirmaster Osgood Lark, Goody Thornapple, the Three Tuns.
Physical Order: Pellam Hobbs, the Swallow of the Rising Court, and the Varūn war-maul, Year 590.
Spiritual Seat: Mother Hester Quill's deathbed auction of her soul at Ambry, Year 604.
Strata: Margrave Rollo Tollen of Kesterby, the Golden Stair (488 to 519), the chanter Wren Maddock, the Ledger Monks of Hallow Reach.
Abyssal Depths: the eruption at Cinderhowe, Year 662; the volcanologist Thessaly Orne.
Glosses and small texture: Scale clergy retire on a corrody; neumes for writing out Sylorin's hum; the Throne-network glossed as the web of binding running up to each Titan's and Archon's seat.

calls.call: Epoch-scale figures stay as written (a Titan's heartbeat per thousand years, Faisal's eleven thousand years of Oath-service). The Titan hub now warns that they are not years on the count.
calls.grounds: Errata Section II: Epoch figures are accurate about magnitude and meaningless as years, and are never placed on the count.

calls.call: The Dawi Tally's six thousand years and the Closing Eye's four thousand years of casting are kept, marked as the holders' own reckoning that the Errata would cut down.
calls.grounds: They exceed the 2,115-year reckoned count, and the Errata withdraws old figures above about two thousand. The brief says no fact is lost, so I flagged them and did not rewrite the numbers.

calls.call: Old-register age names are kept with an in-place note: Pyrrhean Epidemic, Era and Calamity (Antediluvian collapse, about -550 to -450), and the Fractured Era (no sealed chronology, read as Divisional opinion).
calls.grounds: Errata Section III substitutions, plus the brief's direction to agree with the Concordance and keep every fact.

calls.call: Thalen's Withering and Maelor's Withering Age are presented as the old Archonic registers' usage, explicitly kept apart from the Withering Era that opens at 645 IC.
calls.grounds: Errata: a register placing the Withering before the Voyager Era is inverted. These events (Echo Vaults later uncovered by the Accord, early Paragons) cannot move to 645 without changing them.

calls.call: Grand World fixes: Gaia's grief now tears rifts across the land where it split continents, and Kaldrion's first continents become first lands, ending in the one body of land the count is written on.
calls.grounds: Brief, Grand World section and Concordance Section VI: one landmass until about 740 IC.

calls.call: The Titans' Ground fields keep their Wellspring names. The hub adds a note that they are written in the same words at larger scale, that Measurewrights argue whether they count among the Sixty, and that each entry's Codex line seats the art on a named one of the Sixty.
calls.grounds: Names like the Wellspring of Strain are not among the fixed Sixty, but the Titan entries and the Sixty are both fixed, so I recorded the tension and altered neither. R83-11 lets Measurewrights argue.

calls.call: The Current keeps its name as the Guild clerks' name, taken from what people say. The page has a Measurewright correct them: what pools is a kind of Aether and nothing runs anywhere.
calls.grounds: R83-9 retires Wellsprings as a current in a pipe, but the faith's name and its folk belief, which it is allowed to be wrong about, should survive.

calls.call: Lease-holders: dead legs and districts the Guild has cut became dead ground with thin ground, walked-off wardens and shut Core keepers. The signal net became fires going dark along the beacon line.
calls.grounds: Brief's retired table and settled terms (beacon line for old wire). The Lease-holders' function and growth measure survive.

calls.call: Throne-network is kept, with a gloss, and the wording around it went from wired and current to tied and handed down.
calls.grounds: The word appears in archived scenes (The Order of Precedence, Paru 86), which are not edited for names.

calls.call: Celestials at tribunal: Vow-Light as the most reliable interrogation method now reads 'where a Celestial can be had at all'. Guild law-enforcement became Guild tribunals and their searchers.
calls.grounds: The same page says only low dozens of sightings exist, so standing tribunal duty needed qualifying. The conscription fact stays.

calls.call: Concord Gates are left named on Pair IV and the Strata page.
calls.grounds: Errata and Concordance date the Gate network to the Voyager Era, The Concord Gate Network is another group's page, and I do not hold the test on it. Whoever holds that page decides.

calls.call: Three quoted in-world epigraphs keep the banned not-X-it-is-Y shape: Faisal's 'not power; it is posture', the Codex of Three Planes, and Chronaeus's 'Time does not pass. It is spent.'
calls.grounds: They are attributed in-world quotations. Only the em dashes changed, and the attributions moved to their own lines.

calls.call: Part Four and the Author Notes on the Faiths page stay out-of-world, as table advice and a real-world research note, with setting fixes only. Part One is turned in-world.
calls.grounds: The brief says nothing is lost, and the research caveat says it belongs on the page.

calls.call: Section headings changed em dashes to colons. H1 titles and page names keep theirs.
calls.grounds: A grep of wiki/ found no heading anchors pointing into these pages, so nothing breaks.

calls.call: Mechanics: a machine check against wiki/ found no wikilink, number or glyph lost, and frontmatter unchanged. Only four rewritten bold phrases differ, all edited deliberately. Greps for retired terms and em dashes are clean apart from ordinary English 'draw' and page names. I had no sound-effect grep hit list, so that check rests on my reading of the openings and originals.
calls.grounds: Verification, reported so the launching session knows what it covers. I did not re-read each finished page top to bottom after the scripted edits, because the task said not to reread what was already read; I read every original whole and wrote every change.

calls.call: Scratchpad slip: the session scratchpad is shared across agents, and my first Write to scratchpad/apply1.py overwrote an existing file of that name that another agent may have made. It cannot be recovered. I moved to scratchpad/faith/ and removed my root copies of apply1.py and applylib.py.
calls.grounds: Disclosed in case another agent's edit script is missing. Staged pages were not touched by this.

canon_conflicts: The Celestial Host, Section I says Malakar took eleven minutes to prove Faisal's personhood could be broken, while Section V says every source agrees Faisal is still kneeling, whole. Both are kept.
Titan Grounds named as Wellsprings (Strain, Form, Breath and others) against the fixed Sixty. Recorded on the Titan hub as a Measurewright argument, not resolved.
Both Valen and Chronaeus carry the epithet 'the Clock of Ages'. Left as they are, since both are fixed.
Great Spirit War and Great Spirit Wars both appeared on the Strata page; normalized to the singular per R83-6.

calls.call: How this group was checked at the end.
calls.grounds: I read all 37 originals whole, then edited them with throwaway scripts in the scratchpad (nothing added to the repo). I did not do a fresh whole read of the finished pages. Instead I reviewed every former em dash site in the War Cycle and ran scripted checks on all 37 against wiki/: wikilinks, embeds, frontmatter and every number are unchanged, and no stray em dashes remain. Greps for retired terms, British spellings and sound words turned up the items fixed or listed here. Artifact em dash sites were not reviewed one by one: the ones I expected to read badly got explicit fixes, the rest took a mechanical comma, so a stray comma splice is possible there.
